item.title: Heat trace and Riesz means with a large Robin parameter
item.description: arXiv:2610.40804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Laplacian with Robin boundary conditions on a smooth Riemannian manifold with boundary and investigate the behavior of various spectral quantities as the Robin parameter approaches infinity. Although the spectrum, heat trace, and Riesz means converge pointwise to their Dirichlet analogues, the asymptotics of these quantities as the spectral parameter approaches infinity, or as time approaches zero, do not. The remainders in the usual asymptotic expansions are not bounded as the Robin parameter approaches infinity. Our main result is a two-term asymptotic expansion for the Robin heat trace that depends jointly on the time variable and the Robin parameter, with a remainder that satisfies a uniform bound independent of the Robin parameter. We apply this result to obtain a similar two-term asymptotic expansion for Riesz means of order at least one, again with a remainder bound independent of the Robin parameter.
item.dc:creator: David A. Sher

item.title: Generic properties of the Laplace spectrum and eigenfunctions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the spectrum of the Laplace--Beltrami operator on compact Riemannian manifolds without boundary is generically linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. Furthermore, we prove that pointwise products of eigenfunctions generically are linearly independent. The proof is based on conformal perturbations of the metric. The result implies in particular that generically the truncation of the continuous functions on $M$ by spectral projections of the Laplace operator is given by symmetric matrices.
item.dc:creator: Oliver F\"urst, Eva-Maria Hekkelman, Malte Leimbach

item.title: Spectral Convergence of the Discrete Steklov Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.40920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Schur complement $\textbf{S}$ of the graph Laplacian, defined on vertices sampled from a domain with $C^2$ boundary. We use a thin boundary layer to approximate the continuum boundary as the number of vertices increases and rely on transportation theory to justify the consistency of a discrete Steklov problem. In particular, $\textbf{S}$ acts on vectors defined over the shrinking boundary layer but behaves asymptotically like a known operator. In this paper, we use a variational argument to determine conditions for which the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $\textbf{S}$ converge to the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a Dirichlet-to-Neumann map, and we provide evidence of this spectral convergence through a numerical example.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Lyons

item.title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.41002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Malo Gatignol, Joe Thomas

item.title: Rigidity in sharp eigenvalue estimates for differential forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.41297v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $1\leq p\leq n/2$, we derive sharp eigenvalue estimates for the Hodge Laplacian on differential $p$-forms under the curvature condition introduced by Petersen and Wink, and study their equality cases. Equality recovers the stronger curvature operator lower bound and, in the closed case, leaves only round or Sasakian metrics on the universal cover. For manifolds with boundary, weak $p$-convexity of the boundary makes the unit hemisphere the only equality case for the absolute boundary problem.
item.dc:creator: Tsz-Kiu Aaron Chow, James Koh, Sen Yuk Wu

item.title: Area laws for free fermions in ergodic field: spectral criteria and localisation-based methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.41845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We review rigorous results concerning the Area Law for the entanglement entropy of free fermions whose one-body Hamiltonian is an ergodic Schr\"odinger operator with a strongly localised pure point spectrum. Particular attention is paid to operators with deterministic potentials (quasi-periodic ones and those generated by subshifts of finite type). Our approach relies on reducing the problem to obtaining exponential estimates for the eigenfunction correlator. This provides an effective route from localisation to the Area Law and allows for the identification of additional spectral estimates that need to be proven for various classes of ergodic operators. We realise this approach by using various localisation techniques, including dynamical localisation and the uniformly localised eigenfunction property for bounded and unbounded ergodic operators (e.g. the Maryland model), as well as a new method for obtaining the corresponding exponential bounds for Schr\"odinger operators generated by subshifts of finite type.
item.dc:creator: Leonid Pastur, Mira Shamis

item.title: Persistence of Unitary Almost Mathieu Operator Gaps Ten Dry Martinis, Five on the Rim
item.description: arXiv:2610.42120v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine exactly which gap labels are realized by open spectral gaps for the unitary almost Mathieu operator at every irrational frequency and all coupling constants ($0<\lambda_1,\lambda_2\leq1$). When both couplings are strictly less than one, every permitted gap label is realized by an open gap, including in the critical case ($\lambda_1=\lambda_2$). When at least one coupling equals one, both lifts of every odd winding label are realized by open gaps, whereas all even winding labels are collapsed. The proof combines quantitative almost reducibility and Aubry duality with a monotonicity principle for gap heights.
item.dc:creator: Dan S. Borgnia, Matthew Faust, Long Li
